summary: We developed SPUD, an intelligent health monitoring system designed to track and safeguard astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. By continuously tracking vital physiological markers and environmental data, SPUD bridges the gap between raw biometric feeds and proactive medical care. It provides crew members and flight surgeons with real-time health insights, early anomaly detection, and automated alerts to mitigate the physical tolls of microgravity. This project is vital because ensuring astronaut health and cognitive readiness is essential for mission success and safety as humanity pushes further into deep space exploration.
details: For SPUD, we built a health monitoring system designed to keep astronauts safe during long-duration space missions. The platform uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to power a clean, low-latency dashboard that crew members can check instantly at a glance, while Python handles the backend data processing and AI models. Together, they pair wearable biosensors with machine learning to track vital signs like heart rate, oxygen levels, and fatigue in real time, automatically flagging microgravity-induced stress before it becomes a serious issue. What makes SPUD unique is its focus on autonomy—it’s designed to operate smoothly even during communication blackouts with Earth while cutting down on false alarms. Ultimately, our goal is to shift space healthcare from reactive treatment to proactive prevention, giving astronauts a reliable safety net as we push further into deep space.
dataRefs: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
